title: Appeal of TE Eliot Lee vs. Korean Eastern Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained. The sole stated issue—whether KEP erred in proceeding to trial of TE Lee—was answered Yes. KEP's disposition and excommunication of TE Lee were reversed and rendered. The SJC also issued pastoral counsel, expressly not a formal censure. Prior adopted panel judgments in 2007-1, 2007-6, 2007-7, 2007-9, and 2007-10 are summarized in the source but are not the 2007-11 issue disposition.
first_summary: The SJC sustained TE Eliot Lee's appeal from Korean Eastern Presbytery's decision to depose and excommunicate him after trial. It reversed because KEP failed to follow BCO procedural requirements for serving the indictment and citations and for giving notice of trial. The SJC used BCO 42-9 to render the decision it believed should have been made and issued pastoral counsel rather than a censure.
summary: After Korean Eastern Presbytery tried, convicted, deposed, and excommunicated TE Eliot Lee, the SJC sustained his appeal and reversed the disposition and excommunication. The decisive reason was procedural: the record did not show timely service of the indictment/citations or the required 14-day trial notice, violating BCO 32-3, 32-7, and 32-10. Under BCO 42-9, the SJC rendered the decision it thought should have been made, finding no strong presumption of guilt under BCO 31-2 justified formal process; it added pastoral counsel, expressly not censure.

sources.supports: Canonical case identity, procedural history, adopted judgments, disposition, reasoning, vote, and incorporated panel decisions.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Lines 1-5, 13, 159-167: SJC case 2007-11, 37th GA (2009), titled Appeal of TE Eliot Lee vs. Korean Eastern Presbytery; facts/issues/judgment/reasoning written by RE Samuel J. Duncan; vote 20 concur, 1 disqualified, 2 absent, no separate opinion.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 61-77, 121-125: KEP judicial commission indicted TE Lee on five charges, tried him 05-29-07, found him guilty on all counts, deposed and excommunicated him; KEP's 73rd Stated Meeting adopted that decision; the appeal issue is whether KEP erred in proceeding to trial.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 123-157: SJC answered Yes; reversed and rendered KEP's disposition and excommunication. Reasons: no evidence of compliance with BCO 32-3 service/timely indictment/citation, BCO 32-7 10-day interval, and BCO 32-3 14-day trial notice, citing BCO 32-10. Under BCO 42-9, SJC rendered the decision; BCO 31-2 no strong presumption of guilt justified formal process; pastoral counsel expressly not formal censure.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 133, 153-157: SJC did not discuss all errors because procedural errors sufficed; pastoral counsel is not a censure; no acquittal on the merits is stated, but the formal disposition/excommunication is reversed. Lines 101: prior judgments on commission appointments were not approval or disapproval of later complained actions.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Lines 77-117: Full SJC adopted panel decisions in 2007-1 (actions at 71st Stated Meeting null/moot), 2007-6 and 2007-7 (interim pastor = stated supply limited by BCO 22-6; pulpit and judicial commissions properly appointed), and 2007-9/2007-10 (pulpit commission actions annulled; KEP erred ratifying executive committee and filing civil action over ecclesiastical matters). These are companion incorporated results, not the 2007-11 issue.

source_limits: Source is an excerpt from GA minutes that includes incorporated summaries of five companion complaints but no full trial transcript, no separate opinions, and no complete exhibit record; it notes the record lacked the citation and second citation. Synopsis is therefore limited to the adopted procedural rulings and stated disposition.
benchmark_examples: A01 (Grady): distinguishes conviction, censure, dissolution, and suspension; here the SJC reversed a deposition/excommunication while issuing non-censuring pastoral counsel.
A19 (Spann): record-limit example; here the synopsis preserves the procedural posture and does not treat the underlying charges as merits acquittal.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged presbytery action—trial, deposition, and excommunication of TE Lee—rather than merely naming the parties.
score_reasons.decision: States the appeal was sustained and the disposition/excommunication reversed; notes pastoral counsel was not censure.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: States the adopted procedural grounds under BCO 32-3, 32-7, and 32-10, plus the BCO 42-9 remedy and BCO 31-2 no-strong-presumption finding.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Captures the limit that procedural defects reversed the discipline without adjudicating all merits and that pastoral counsel is not formal censure.
score_reasons.fidelity: Keeps the appeal disposition distinct from KEP's trial verdict, the prior incorporated complaints, and the non-censuring pastoral counsel.
score_reasons.economy: All retained details explain the procedural error, reversal, or remedy; no filing chronology or extraneous background.
